current: \label{sec:prr} A study specified in advance tests which settings of the five-observable estimator change the fraction of a truth change that remains unrecovered.
It uses noise-free pseudo-data with backgrounds at one split of the simulation and measures the retained fraction $\rho=-\sum_c b_c d_c/\sum_c d_c^2$ at each graded truth.
Here $d_c=(X_c-P_c)/P_c$ is the truth's departure from the prior in cell $c$ and $b_c=(\hat X_c-X_c)/P_c$ is the bias, with $\hat X$, $X$ and $P$ the unfolded, true and prior cross sections.
The sums run over cells where $|d_c|$ is at least \SI{1}{\percent}; $\rho=1$ if the result is the prior and $\rho=0$ if the departure is recovered.
The study changes one setting at a time: the iteration count, classifier capacity, training statistics or observables used by the classifiers.
It also runs an exact binned IBU on the same pseudo-data.
A tested level clears a flagged truth if the truth is no longer flagged under the criterion of section~\ref{sec:strategy} applied to the noise-free pseudo-data.

At the two flagged truths, each setting is classified by whether any tested level moves $\rho$ from the reported configuration's value by more than a threshold fixed in advance: \emph{increases} if some level raises it by more than the threshold and none lowers it that far, \emph{reduces} in the reverse case, \emph{both} if each happens, and \emph{no effect} if no level moves it that far.
A class names no direction of the setting: \emph{increases} is assigned whether the level that raises $\rho$ lies above or below the reported setting.
A separate test asks whether the IBU's retained fraction falls or rises by at least a fixed margin of 0.05, distinct from that threshold, between five and 200 iterations.

The results are combined into labels fixed in advance: consistent with finite-iteration regularization (some tested iteration count reduces $\rho$, and the IBU's retained fraction falls with more iterations); consistent with an information limit at these settings (no tested iteration count or capacity reduces $\rho$, and the IBU's does not fall); and consistent with a share specific to the implementation (the IBU at five iterations has a lower $\rho$ than the five-observable estimator, or some tested capacity reduces $\rho$).
The study selects no estimator; its results describe these truths only (\ssec{S9}{supp:tests}).
